title: Jump Game II
statement: You start at index 0. `nums[i]` is the maximum jump length from i. Return the minimum number of jumps to reach the last index. A solution always exists.
hints: BFS layers on the index line: from the current jump's range, the next range is the farthest you can reach.
You do not need the actual indices, only the end of the current jump window and the farthest index seen inside it.
When the scan index hits the end of the window, you must jump, so increment the count and extend the window to the farthest index.

approaches.name: DP
approaches.explanation: dp[i] is the minimum jumps to reach i.

editorial: The linear scan is BFS on a line. current_end is the farthest index reachable with the jumps already committed. farthest is the farthest index reachable with one more jump. When i equals current_end and i is not the last index, commit one jump and set current_end to farthest.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def jump(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    jumps = current_end = farthest = 0
    for i in range(len(nums) - 1):
        farthest = max(farthest, i + nums[i])
        if i == current_end:
            jumps += 1
            current_end = farthest
    return jumps

examples.explanation: Two jumps: index 0 to 1, then to the end.
